name: Clarinet
description: A soft reed in the style of a clarinet, bass clarinet, subtone saxophone or duduk: hollow and woody, breathy when quiet and brighter the harder it is blown.

params.name: Bore
params.description: The shape of the pipe. Low is a clarinet's cylinder, hollow with every other overtone missing; high is a saxophone's cone, fuller and more vocal.

params.name: Blow
params.description: How hard the reed is blown. Low is a pure, soft hum; high is a bright, reedy tone that opens up as each note swells.

params.name: Breath
params.description: Air heard under the tone, coloured by the pipe. High with Blow low is a subtone, more breath than note.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long a note takes to speak. Short is a tongued start; long fades in from nothing, air first. Low notes always speak a little later than high ones.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long a note takes to fade once the key is let go. The tone darkens as it goes and the air lingers a moment after it.

params.name: Vibrato
params.description: Depth of a slow pitch vibrato that arrives a moment after the note starts. At zero the note is held straight.

params.name: Growl
params.description: A fast flutter in the breath that makes the tone rasp. At zero the tone is smooth.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit, after the single-reed family (B flat and bass clarinet, tenor and alto saxophone, duduk) as described in the acoustic research for this instrument. It is an open-loop driven pipe: one phase per voice drives a closed-form harmonic series whose brightness is proportional to the level of the tone (Worman's power law for reed instruments), Bore runs from the odd harmonics of a cylinder to the full series of a cone, and breath noise passes a feedback comb that stands in for the passive pipe. Simplified: no reed and no bore are simulated, there is no register key, and the body is a fixed equaliser. Choices, not measurements of an instrument: the 1.5 kHz tone-hole cutoff above which the even harmonics return, the tone following the square of the breath while the noise follows the breath itself, the 6 cent lean of pitch against level, the speech time of eight periods, the 5 Hz vibrato, the 28 Hz growl and the body curve. Not a circuit or sample emulation.
